title: Harden sshd: localhost bind, key before listen
head: 89e20be1ae3b
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: On first setup without host keys, validation fails before the service can generate them
leads.consequence: OpenSSH's sshd -t/-T loads host keys and exits 1 when none exist. Arch's sshdgenkeys.service generates them as a WantedBy dependency of sshd.service, but this PR now calls sshd -t twice before starting that service. With a newly installed or never-started sshd and no host keys, the first check deletes the new localhost file, the second deletes hardening and exits 1 under set -e; the service never starts, and the user's key remains authorized. Previously setup_sshd started the service before sshd -t. Generate host keys before checking, without starting a listener, and test that state.

leads.summary: A previously configured public ListenAddress remains public after the loopback drop-in
leads.consequence: OpenSSH queues every ListenAddress, resolves and appends them, then listens on all entries. An existing administrator drop-in specifying a concrete external interface IP remains effective alongside the PR's 127.0.0.1 and ::1. A later wildcard ListenAddress can also bind first and outcompete loopback on that port (socket overlap makes bind order significant). sshd -t accepts the directives, and the command announces localhost only despite the externally bound socket. An earlier wildcard can instead lose the bind race to loopback, so it is not an unconditional example. A preexisting open UFW rule makes it remotely reachable. Detect effective listen addresses or refuse/describe conflicting user rules instead of assuming the additional file narrows them.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3 additive ListenAddress); corroboration

leads.summary: AddressFamily=inet/inet6 makes the hardcoded dual-family drop-in fail open
leads.consequence: With an administrator's AddressFamily inet, ::1 cannot resolve under AF_INET (analogously 127.0.0.1 under inet6), so the first sshd -t fails. bind_localhost deletes its file and returns success; disable_password_auth validates the remaining configuration and start_sshd proceeds, without a loopback bind. On a previously running daemon or an existing open firewall rule this leaves the public listener in place while announcing localhost only. Treat a rejected bind as fatal, and accommodate one-family hosts rather than silently falling back.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3 AddressFamily rollback); corroboration

leads.summary: Moving key validation before the openssh installation makes the install path unable to bootstrap itself
leads.consequence: On a machine where openssh was removed or not yet installed, ssh-keygen is missing because openssh supplies it. Every --key, pasted-key and GitHub-key route now fails validation before omarchy-pkg-add openssh is reached, so rerunning cannot install the server; earlier ordering installed openssh first. Ensure the key validator is available before its call without enabling the daemon.

leads.summary: Global sshd -T does not prove password auth is off for matched users
leads.consequence: PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractiveAuthentication are allowed inside Match blocks. A later administrator Match User <account> with PasswordAuthentication yes overrides the globally effective no after connection selection, while sudo sshd -T without -C prints no and the script reports password logins off and starts sshd. If the listener is reachable through existing rules, this user can still authenticate by password. This global-only check predates the PR, but its key-only-before-first-listen guarantee still depends on it; test a user-specific -T -C case or state the limit.
leads.triage: pre-existing validator gap (global sshd -T vs Match User), not introduced by this PR; not published

leads.summary: A fingerprint-valid authorized key need not be a usable SSH login
leads.consequence: An existing administrator setting such as PubkeyAuthentication no or AuthorizedKeysFile none, or a matched version of either, makes the key appended to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys unusable. ssh-keygen -lf still accepts it; the script checks only password/kbdinteractive in sshd -T, then starts sshd, disables passwords and says the key is authorized. New remote connections cannot use that key and may have no login method. This was also a preexisting check gap, now a premise of the changed key-before-listen guarantee. Verify the daemon's effective pubkey and authorized-key settings for the actual account before claiming access.
leads.triage: pre-existing validator gap (PubkeyAuthentication/AuthorizedKeysFile), not introduced by this PR; not published

leads.summary: Upgraded SSH installs stay public, and old UFW rules survive a re-run
leads.consequence: An existing machine configured by the previous setup already has sshd enabled on public interfaces and the 'omarchy-sshd' UFW 22/tcp limit rule. This PR adds no migration for the new 20-omarchy-localhost.conf, so merely upgrading leaves that old public listener and rule intact. Even if the user reruns setup to write the bind, open_firewall only prints messages and never removes or inspects the old rule; 'SSH firewall port left closed' is false, and a later bind change/removal instantly restores remote reachability. Migrate the existing installs or scope the claim to fresh setups, and close only the Omarchy-owned legacy rule rather than user rules.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2 no migration, stale ufw rule on re-run); corroboration

leads.summary: Update the opt-in SSH acceptance test for the new closed-firewall policy
leads.consequence: When run on a clean VM with UFW present and no old 22 rule, the opt-in acceptance test calls the modified setup and then requires `ufw status` to contain `22/tcp LIMIT`. The new setup never creates that rule, so the acceptance suite fails even after the host-key bootstrap is repaired. Assert the intended closed rule and effective listener instead.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2 acceptance test); coordinator read test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh:92-94

leads.summary: The remove command never removes the newly created localhost drop-in
leads.consequence: Setup creates /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/20-omarchy-localhost.conf; removal only disables sshd, deletes a UFW limit rule, optionally deletes authorized_keys. A later manual re-enable or alternate service startup still binds loopback, even though 'remove SSH server access' implies cleaning managed setup; re-running setup always recreates the file after a user followed the in-file instructions to remove it to expose SSH. Add explicit lifecycle handling or clearly document preservation.
leads.triage: already in Opus related work; coordinator read omarchy-remove-security-sshd; published in F2 list

leads.summary: The success message suggests remote SSH although the new default refuses it
leads.consequence: After successful loopback-only configuration the final line still says 'You can now connect with: ssh $USER@$(hostname)'. From another host that cannot reach a loopback-bound sshd and a default-deny UFW, the suggested command fails. Print a local-only command (or explain the opt-in remote procedure) rather than promising remote access.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2 success message)

leads.summary: The CLI command summary still advertises opening the firewall
leads.consequence: The command's omarchy:summary says it opens the firewall, while new open_firewall leaves 22 closed. `omarchy setup security sshd --help` and the command list display this stale summary, so users expecting a reachable SSH server receive the opposite behavior. Update this metadata along with the help already changed.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2 summary metadata)

leads.summary: Networking manual still says setup opens port 22
leads.consequence: The published Networking > firewall instructions tell users Setup > Security > SSHD starts sshd and opens port 22, but new code binds loopback and leaves UFW closed. Update this page with the default and the remote opt-in steps, or its instructions leave users unable to reach the new server.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); coordinator read manual/35-networking.md:33

leads.summary: Security manual still says setup opens port 22
leads.consequence: The published Security page describes the setup menu as opening and rate-limiting port 22. It now leaves the port closed and only accepts localhost SSH, so the advertised remote-access step no longer works. Update this separate page and include remote opt-in guidance.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); coordinator read manual/48-security.md:6

leads.summary: The new ordering assertion passes when startup is moved before both drop-ins
leads.consequence: A controlled mutant moved `start_sshd` between install_openssh and bind_localhost, before both configuration writes; every new test still passed with LC_ALL=C, including 'starts sshd only after hardening is in place'. Presence of enable --now in the call log is not an order assertion. The omarchy-cmd-missing stub always reports ufw absent even though install/omarchy-base.packages:135 ships it, so no new installed-UFW message branch is exercised either. Log install/config writes and systemctl in one chronological trace, assert the daemon is enabled last, and exercise both UFW-present and absent branches.
leads.triage: new detail; coordinator verified Sol sealed run mutant-plan/runs/20260927T133123Z-6a8f92e7 (status 0, 6 ok, seal verified); Opus reproduced in plan3/runs/20260927T135439Z-0c9012e9; published in test table

leads.summary: Coordinate this ordering/bind change with the open key-only SSH rewrite
leads.consequence: Open PR #9463 rewrites the same setup path into a root machine phase, and #9474 includes that implementation. Neither is stacked with this head. comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the key-before-listen reordering closes the gap from #8363. With `--key=not-a-key`, a cancelled menu or paste prompt, an empty or invalid paste, an empty GitHub username, a failed GitHub fetch, or GitHub keys that are all invalid, the head exits 1 before anything is installed, written or started. Base had already started sshd on all addresses with password login on, and run `ufw limit 22/tcp`, before failing on those paths. When host keys already exist, the first start at head already has `PasswordAuthentication no`.

The main issue is that the new order fails on machines where sshd has never started. The loopback-only default is also a larger behavior change than the rest of the repository reflects.

### Setup fails when sshd has never started (no host keys yet)

`sshd -t` and `sshd -T` now run before the first `systemctl enable --now sshd.service`. OpenSSH exits early when no host key loads (`sshd.c` at V_10_5_P1, "no hostkeys available -- exiting."), before either check completes. On Arch, host keys are created only by `sshdgenkeys.service` (`ssh-keygen -A`), which `sshd.service` pulls in through `Wants=`/`After=` when it starts. Omarchy ships sshd disabled, and factory reset deletes the host keys (`bin/omarchy-system-factory-reset`).

```text
base                                  head
enable --now sshd  -> host keys made  authorize key
ufw limit 22/tcp                      bind_localhost: sshd -t   -> exit 1, drop-in removed
authorize key                         disable_password_auth: sshd -t -> exit 1, removed
sshd -t / sshd -T  -> pass            (start_sshd never reached)  -> exit 1
reload             -> exit 0
```

Observed in an isolated run with real OpenSSH 10.5p1 against a private config tree, all privileged commands stubbed, and the unit's key-generation step modelled: with a valid key through `--key`, `--gh-keys` or paste, the head prints "sshd rejected the localhost bind config; removing it." and then "sshd rejected the hardening config; removing it and leaving passwords on.", exits 1, and never enables sshd. Base exits 0 in the same scenarios. Once host keys exist, the head flow succeeds. This was not run on a real VM with systemd.

**Impact:** Setup > Security > SSHD fails on fresh installs and after a factory reset, wherever sshd has not run yet, and its messages blame the drop-ins rather than the missing host keys. The shell test cannot see this because its `sshd` stub accepts `-t` whether or not sshd has started or host keys exist. The same constraint was raised by the bot on closed PR #8365.

**Suggested change:** generate host keys before validating, for example `sudo systemctl start sshdgenkeys.service` (the unit `sshd.service` itself pulls in) or `sudo ssh-keygen -A`, then validate, then `enable --now`.

### Loopback-only default removes remote access; the rest of the repository still assumes it

After setup, sshd listens only on `127.0.0.1:22` and `[::1]:22`, yet the command still ends with "You can now connect with: ssh $USER@$(hostname)". Re-running it on a machine that is already set up writes the drop-in and reloads sshd. Established sessions survive the reload, but new connections from other machines are refused, and the command prints "SSH firewall port left closed" although the earlier `ufw limit 22/tcp` rule is still in place.

Places that still describe or depend on remote access:

- `omarchy:summary` (line 3) still says "open the firewall". The help text says "by default", but no option selects anything else.
- `manual/35-networking.md` and `manual/48-security.md` say the setup opens port 22.
- `test/acceptance.d/security-test.sh` asserts a `22/tcp LIMIT` ufw rule when ufw is present, so it fails with this change (read, not run).
- `plans/server.md` relies on this command for a machine that is reachable before first login.
- `migrations/1788124236.sh` tells users with sshd enabled to run this command, which would now switch their server to loopback.
- `bin/omarchy-remove-security-sshd` does not remove the new `20-omarchy-localhost.conf`.
- The omarchy-iso test harness reaches the VM over forwarded guest port 22 with a new connection per call, so artifact collection after the acceptance suite would likely be refused (inferred from omarchy-iso source, not run).

**Impact:** the command that exists to enable SSH access produces a server no other machine can reach. For #8248, the omarchy-iso unattended path still enables sshd on all interfaces with `ufw allow ssh`, and existing machines are not migrated, so "Fixes #8248" covers only this opt-in command.

**Suggested change:** whether loopback should be the default is a maintainer decision. If it is, update the summary, success message, manuals, acceptance test, removal command and callers above together. If not, keep remote access as the default and offer loopback as an explicit option.

### "Localhost bind only" is printed without being checked

- When `sshd -t` rejects the new drop-in, `bind_localhost` removes it and returns 0, and setup continues. With an existing `AddressFamily inet`, OpenSSH rejects `ListenAddress ::1`. In the isolated run (ufw present) the command exited 0 and printed "localhost bind only" while sshd's effective config (`sshd -T`) listed only `0.0.0.0:22`.
- `ListenAddress` entries accumulate rather than first-wins (`servconf.c`). An existing `ListenAddress 0.0.0.0` in any drop-in still gives `0.0.0.0:22` plus loopback, and the same message is printed.
- When ufw is absent, `open_firewall` now prints nothing; the old "UFW is not installed" line is gone.

**Impact:** the command can report a loopback-only server while sshd's effective config still listens on all addresses.

**Suggested change:** check the effective listeners with `sshd -T` (as is already done for password settings), and report or fail when they are not loopback-only.

### A failed re-run leaves the loopback drop-in for the next restart

The `20-` drop-in is written before `disable_password_auth`, and nothing removes it when that step fails. In the isolated run, a re-run on an active server with an existing administrator `PasswordAuthentication yes` exited 1 and left the `20-` drop-in on disk without a reload. Base leaves no Omarchy drop-in behind in the same scenario.

**Impact:** the next sshd restart (a reboot, or Arch's `70-openssh-restart-sshd.hook` on an openssh upgrade) would apply loopback-only without notice, after a run that reported failure.

**Suggested change:** remove the `20-` drop-in when a later step fails, or write it only after `disable_password_auth` succeeds and reload an already-running sshd after writing it (the existing reload inside `disable_password_auth` would then run too early).

**Key validation before install:** `valid_key` uses `ssh-keygen`, which comes from the `openssh` package that is now installed only after the key step. Stock Omarchy already has openssh, so this matters only where it is missing: there, a valid key is rejected (simulated by removing `ssh-keygen` from PATH until the package stub runs), so setup cannot proceed. Suggested change: call `install_openssh` before the key step; installing the package does not start sshd.

**Optional test improvement:** the repository test passes at head (6 checks) and at base, and the head test does fail against the base script, so the reordering is detected. Three gaps showed up with mutants of the head script:

| Mutant | Head test |
|---|---|
| `start_sshd` moved after the key step but before `bind_localhost` and `disable_password_auth` | passes all 6 checks, despite the "starts sshd only after hardening" assertion |
| sshd already running is never reloaded | passes: no case sets `SSHD_ACTIVE=1` |
| `sudo ufw allow 22/tcp` added before the key step | passes |

The runtime firewall assertion cannot fail: no stub logs ufw calls, and the `omarchy-cmd-missing` stub always reports ufw as missing. The static grep only matches the literal `sudo ufw limit 22` spelling. Checking call order in the log (drop-ins before `enable --now`, which needs the `sudo` stub to log `install` calls), adding an `SSHD_ACTIVE=1` case, and a ufw stub that logs, with `omarchy-cmd-missing` reporting ufw as present in at least one case, would cover these.

**Related work:** open drafts #9463 and #9474 (#9474 contains #9463) rewrite the same setup path with the same ordering goal and conflict with this PR in both files. #9307 conflicts in the script and #9506 in the test.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** head `89e20be1`, with both changed files unchanged on the current `quattro`. Repository shell test, head/base cross runs, test mutants, real `sshd -t`/`-T` (OpenSSH 10.5p1) and end-to-end head and base runs of the script, all in an isolated sandbox with privileged, network and firewall commands stubbed. Host-key generation was modelled from the Arch unit files; no VM or real systemd, and no network listeners. The acceptance test and omarchy-iso harness were read, not run. IPv6-disabled kernels were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
